reason: The eight children each discuss an aspect of the intermediate state at length, citing scripture, refuting opposing views and answering objections.
The first child explains the twelve links in detail with objections and replies and the second argues the nature of ignorance with examples, though the third is only a pointer to the root verses.
The children define, classify and analyse the four foods with citations, illustrative stories and a debate about whom giving food is most meritorious.
The children give extended descriptions of the four continents, the eight subcontinents and the special features of Jambudvipa with scriptural citations.
The children give long expositions of the sun and moon mansions and the terraces of Mount Meru, with measurements, competing views and citations.
